name: IA que acumula
meta: Build a working foundation with AI that preserves what you learn. Watch the six videos and start with the free kit for context, repositories, and proof.
hero: Your next agent can pick up where you left off.
lead: What you learn today can become a capability of your own tomorrow. With an evolving Jarvis, you bring together context, make use of good components, and improve your system without starting over with every tool.
summary: A Jarvis is a personal AI assistant that you organize for your work. IA que acumula is a study and practice kit for anyone who wants to start their own assistant or improve the agents they already use. It helps you save instructions in files, study one item in a project folder, and check a small task. That way, you can reuse your setup when you switch tools. The videos explain the idea before the technical details; the exercise uses an agent you already have.
videoIntro: Choose the starting point that suits you. There are six independent videos, all in Portuguese, organized in two rounds. Each one stands on its own.
round1: Build your Jarvis and preserve what you learn
round2Note: The competition for professionals after 2027 is Nei’s view of a possible scenario, with no guarantee of employment or income.

methodTitle: The tool changes. Your foundation can stay.
methodIntro: Building your own system means understanding the role of its components and learning how to combine them. You can use existing projects and third-party services. You don’t need to write every library or train a model from scratch.
simulationTitle: Switch the tool. See what stays.
simulationNote: Visual simulation: the button switches the agent and keeps the same context. This demonstration does not run artificial intelligence.
toolDetail: Repositories and tools you have studied
proofDetail: An example with an expected result
graphTitle: Acceleration is why learning to adapt matters
graphNote: The exponential curve is a conceptual illustration in Portuguese, with no numerical scale, dates, or measured forecast. It represents the idea of acceleration; it does not show that every AI capability grows this way.
graphAlt: Conceptual curve of AI acceleration, with a modular personal assistant and a closed platform in the background
actionIntro: Start with a task you know. In the kit’s fictional example, Ana needs to review a proposal by sexta. Bruno needs to confirm a meeting, but did not provide a deadline.
action1Text: Ask for a list with a person, task, and deadline. Explain what needs to appear before choosing a tool.
action2Title: Build a foundation of your own
action2Text: Save the context and instructions in readable files. When you find a useful component, study its origin, license, and a small adaptation.
action3Title: Check and save what you learn
action3Text: Bruno’s deadline must remain pendente. If the agent invents a date, correct the rule and rerun the test. Only a confirmed improvement goes into memory.
enterpriseTitle: Taking the idea to a company
enterpriseText: Show a well-defined problem, a working demonstration, and how the result was checked. Compare the entire process, including time spent reviewing and correcting. The kit’s executive brief helps organize this pilot; only report gains after measuring them.
technicalTitle: The kit: turn the idea into your first exercise
technicalNote: You don’t need this section to understand the videos and the proposal above.
kitIntro: The program runs locally, with no external dependencies or network calls. It organizes the work of an existing agent; it does not include an AI model or the integrations of a complete Jarvis. A repository is a project folder; a hash identifies a file’s contents and is used to recognize the version that was checked.
cap1: Creates a folder with a goal, context, rules, memory, and a fictional task.
cap2: Records documents and hashes from a local repository for review, without installing or running its code.
cap3: Checks four markers in the Ana/Bruno exercise and saves a receipt with the output hash. A new case needs new proof.
requirementsText: To run the kit, use Python 3.10 or later and a terminal. For the AI portion, use an agent you already have access to. The commands below use python3, which is common on Linux and macOS; on Windows, replace that beginning with py -3. The kit program does not require an API key.
step1Title: Download and open the project folder
step1Text: Download the ZIP, extract it, and open a terminal in the folder containing jarvis.py. If you prefer to use Git, these commands get the same code:
step2Text: Choose a new folder. The program refuses to overwrite an existing destination. The second command creates a request with context you can read and give to your agent.
step3Title: Give the task to the agent you already use
step3Text: Open the meu-jarvis folder in your agent, or copy the contents of pedido.txt into the chat you already use. Ask: read AGENTS.md and TAREFA.md, organize the tasks, and save the result in resultado.md. If you’re using a chat on its own, copy the response into a file named resultado.md inside the meu-jarvis folder. Then check the two lines against the source.
expectedTitle: Expected output for the fictional example
expectedNote: The names, tasks, and values sexta and pendente are literal values from the exercise and remain in Portuguese in all three languages.
step4Text: Run the checker after saving the response in resultado.md. It needs to find Ana, Bruno, sexta associated with Ana, and pendente associated with Bruno. Exit code 0 means it found these markers; this is not a general validation of any AI response.
step5Title: Study a component from a repository
step5Text: Use a repository already on your machine. Replace /caminho/do/repo with the actual path. The record waits for review; ask the agent to explain the requirements, license, and a small change before installing or running anything.
testText: The seven tests check file preservation, context package, incorporation without execution, safe names, a repository without a README, a symbolic link, and the positive/negative example. The published package was also extracted and run in a clean folder.
sourcesText: The method and scenarios are Nei Maldaner’s own perspective. INEMA.club brings together public courses and projects; INEMA.PRO organizes learning paths and curation. The six videos were made for the requested channels: Lives11, Lives7, and Lives3, two for each.
